title: Production comedy script
script: I built OpenClaw to be your personal assistant, on every device and in every chat. Naturally, setup begins with enough configuration to qualify as a minor pilgrimage. It handles messages, email, and travel, then sends the API bill like a tiny financial adviser. We began as Warelay, became ClawdBot, became Moltbot, and finally OpenClaw — because the assistant needed more identity development than its users. Now thirty contributors maintain a very large lobster. Perfectly normal.

title: Production comedy script
script: I built OpenClaw because I wanted a personal assistant on my devices and in my chats. Then I gave it access to messages, email, travel, and every configuration layer known to modern civilisation. People said setup was intimidating, so we simplified it by adding more platforms. People feared the bill, so we made the assistant work harder. Now one lobster-sized project has hundreds of thousands of admirers and thirty contributors. Personal assistant, apparently. Personal staffing crisis.

title: Production comedy script
script:
I built OpenClaw to be your personal assistant, everywhere: messages, email, travel, the lot. It started as Warelay, became Clawdbot, then Moltbot, and finally settled on OpenClaw — because apparently even the name needed an onboarding journey.

It runs across devices and chats, with Android, iOS, plugins, skills, and configuration layers. Simple setup, in the same way assembling a lobster is simple.

The codebase is 90% TypeScript, so naturally the remaining 10% handles the emotional support. I call that personal automation.
